papers.title: Asymptotic Dimension of Persistence Modules of Bounded Presentation
papers.abstract: We compute the asymptotic dimension of spaces of multiparameter persistence modules of bounded presentation under the interleaving distance. The $d$-parameter modules with at most $n$ generators and $m$ relations have asymptotic dimension, and Assouad-Nagata dimension, exactly $d(n+m)$, the number of coordinates of their generator and relation grades, over every field; for two parameters this is $2(n+m)$. The space has continuous moduli, already for two parameters and $n,m\ge2$: over an infinite field it contains, at every scale, infinite uniformly separated families of pairwise non-isomorphic modules with one fibered barcode, so it is not doubling even at a fixed fibered barcode; already for $m\ge1$ it is not coarsely equivalent to a proper metric space. The proof is an induction on the number of distinct grade coordinates: an interleaving small compared with the gaps between these coordinates moves each of them by at most twice its size and preserves the induced grid representation, so the continuous moduli are invisible at large scale. Each class of modules at finite distance therefore embeds coarsely into Hilbert space; for two parameters, $n,m\ge2$ and an uncountable field, a class containing such a family admits no coarse embedding into a separable Hilbert space. Under the two-parameter matching distance, on the space of rank invariants, the asymptotic dimension and the Assouad-Nagata dimension are again $2(n+m)$: slope-one slices pin the grid of grades, and over a grid only finitely many rank invariants occur; on a finite net of $S$ slices the asymptotic dimension is at most $2nS$.

papers.title: Distance algebras of finite distributive lattices are Gorenstein
papers.abstract: Distance algebras were introduced by Asao and Ivanov to realize magnitude homology and cohomology of quasi-metric spaces as Tor- and Ext-groups respectively. Let $\Sigma_L$ be the distance algebra of the Hasse graph of a finite distributive lattice $L$, where the metric is given by the lengths of shortest paths in the graph. We show that $\Sigma_L$ is Gorenstein over any Gorenstein commutative noetherian ring $R$, and give bound of its self-injective dimension. The proof constructs, for each indecomposable (relative) injective module, a projective resolution that is in general non-minimal. When $R=\Bbbk$ is a field, we use algebraic Morse theory to reduce it to a minimal resolution, so that the Betti numbers can be obtained as the dimensions of homologies of certain order complexes. As a consequence, we show that the self-injective dimension of $\Sigma_L$ is the maximal Castelnuovo--Mumford regularity of certain Stanley--Reisner rings. We also show that the first two terms of these minimal resolutions are multiplicity-free, whereas arbitrarily large multiplicities occur in every higher degree. In the appendix, we include a more abstract formulation of the non-minimal projective resolution, namely, a simplicial replacement of a diagram of projective modules.

papers.title: The profinite shape equivalence
papers.abstract: We show that, for every $\infty$-topos $\mathcal{X}$, the profinite shape induces a canonical equivalence between the $\infty$-category of pro-objects in locally constant constructible sheaves of anima in $\mathcal{X}$ and the slice $\infty$-category of profinite anima over the profinite shape $\widehat{\Pi}_{\infty}(\mathcal{X})$. We deduce this profinite shape equivalence from the monodromy classification theorem by establishing a continuous version of the straightening-unstraightening equivalence for profinite anima. In addition, we explain how the monodromy classification theorem recovers its classical counterparts concerning locally constant sheaves of finite sets and of (abelian) groups.

papers.title: Associative Log Rings and their Bimodules
papers.abstract: We propose a definition of associative log rings. The role of the commutative monoid is replaced by a variant of a crossed module whose source is a monoid, and we use the resulting group action to control the failure of commutativity. This extends the classical notion of a log ring, even in the commutative case. Natural examples include algebras of logarithmic differential operators. The definition lends itself to a canonical construction of a log enveloping algebra and hence of log bimodules, and we prove that the resulting second log Hochschild cohomology group classifies log square-zero extensions. Along the way, we complete the logarithmic analog of Quillen's classification of abelian group objects in augmented algebras: In exact augmented associative log rings, abelian group objects recover log bimodules. Our constructions enjoy animated analogs, and we develop the basic theory of associative animated log rings \emph{en route} to our classification of exact log square-zero extensions.

papers.title: Enriched nerves, interleaving distances and the multiplicative magnitude-path spectral sequence
papers.abstract: By regarding the nerves of categories enriched over a monoidal poset as persistence simplicial sets, we investigate an upper bound of the interleaving distance in the homotopy category between the nerves in the sense of Lanary and Scoccola. In particular, it holds that the distance between the nerves for $r$-homotopy equivalent generalized metric spaces is less than or equal to the half of $r$. Moreover, a product on the cochain complex associated with a persistence simplicial set is introduced and related to the cup product on the magnitude cochain complex in the sense of Hepworth. As a consequence, the product gives the multiplicative structure to the cohomological magnitude-path spectral sequence (MPSS) whose first term is isomorphic to the magnitude cohomology ring. Furthermore, we discuss at which term the MPSS for a connected finite digraph collapses by using the interleaving of the enriched nerve of the digraph.

papers.title: Complete characterization of graphs with common maximal abelian cover
papers.abstract: The maximal abelian cover of a connected graph is the quotient of its universal cover by the commutator subgroup of its fundamental group. We provide a complete classification of finite connected graphs with isomorphic maximal abelian covers. For trees or for connected graphs with at least two cycles, the cover determines the base up to isomorphism; in cycle rank one, it determines the primitive cyclic pattern of rooted trees attached to the unique cycle. We also characterize when every automorphism descends to the base and give an orbit-size criterion for splitting the canonical lift extension, answering two questions raised by Baez in 2026.

papers.title: A bordism perspective on ends of manifolds
papers.abstract: We refine the classical pro-homotopy type of the end of a manifold by recording the boundaries of a compact exhaustion together with the bordisms between them. We show that this assignment, the bordism-end, is functorial in embeddings, and independent of the choice of exhaustion. Its target is the free sequential colimit completion of the bordism $\infty$-category. Along the way of defining the bordism-end, we show that the category of all smooth $d$-dimensional manifolds and embeddings is formally obtained from the analogous category of compact manifolds. Through the formalism of the bordism-end, it follows that a manifold is diffeomorphic to the interior of a compact manifold if and only if its bordism-end is representable. Moreover, this formalism yields a fibre sequence relating the classifying spaces of the compactly supported diffeomorphism group of a manifold and its full diffeomorphism group, and a space of bordism-ends. Finally, we set up the pro-end functorially in embeddings, with target the cospan $\infty$-category of pro-spaces, and show that it factors through the bordism-end.

papers.title: Higher orbifold Euler characteristics of torus representations
papers.abstract: We compute the $\Gamma$-Euler characteristic of a finite-dimensional representation of the compact torus $\mathbb{T}^k$ where $\Gamma$ is an arbitrary finitely presented group. We additionally compute the $\Gamma$-Euler characteristic of the unit sphere in such a representation as well as the corresponding symplectic quotient at a nonzero level of the moment map. In each case, the $\Gamma$-Euler characteristic is expressed in terms of the weight matrix for the representation as well as a description of the abelianization of $\Gamma$.

papers.title: Polynomiality ideals, with applications to polynomial functors over free nilpotent groups
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be a unital commutative ring. For a monoidal category $C$ whose unit is a zero object, we introduce a descending filtration of the k-linearization of $C$ by two-sided ideals, called the polynomiality ideals: the $d$-th ideal encodes polynomiality of degree at most $d$ for functors from $C$ to $k$-modules. These ideals yield general criteria for the existence of polynomial functors of a given degree and for equivalences between the categories of polynomial functors of degree at most $d$ over different base categories. For Lawvere theories satisfying a mild condition, we identify the polynomiality ideals with powers of augmentation ideals of monoids; this identification makes the criteria computable by means of classical group ring theory. As the main application, we study polynomial functors over finitely generated free nilpotent groups, comparing them across nilpotency classes and polynomial degrees. We obtain refinements of results of Baues and Pirashvili in the case of class at most 2, recover several folklore results for free groups and free abelian groups, and establish a modular analogue formulated with dimension subgroups over a field of positive characteristic in place of the lower central series. Finally, we show that, in contrast to polynomial functors, analytic functors admit no analogous ideal in most cases.
